decision.note: Infrastructure is useful and should improve, but it should not displace higher-priority product/research work.

strengths: Public/private portfolio boundary is explicit and registry validation enforces public-only records.
Priority score is documented as an attention-allocation score rather than a quality score.
Structured audit sidecars, a rubric, validator, public evidence collector, and metadata-aware freshness checker are now integrated.
The Pages workbench surfaces audit Current/Stale state and open P0/P1 counts without conflating them with portfolio priority.
Audit freshness is exact-SHA by default and only permits explicit, per-audit metadata-only current-equivalent exceptions.
Evidence collector and freshness behavior have deterministic fixture tests in CI.
docs/ is the single canonical Pages source and the retired bootstrap archive has been removed.
Long Gate audit is dogfooding the structured audit and remediation workflow.

findings.title: The repository has no explicit LICENSE
evidence: No LICENSE file was present in the repository root at the audited commit.
findings.recommendation: Choose and add an explicit license before encouraging third-party reuse. This is an owner/legal choice and should not be inferred automatically.

findings.title: Audit results are not surfaced in the GitHub Pages workbench
evidence: docs/app.js loads structured audit sidecars for repositories with latest_audit.
The workbench displays Audit Current/Stale/Current* state plus open P0/P1 counts and links to the audit report.
Pages deployment succeeded on the remediated baseline.
findings.recommendation: Keep audit severity visually and semantically separate from portfolio priority as the UI evolves.

findings.title: No audit staleness detection exists yet
evidence: scripts/audit_freshness.py compares audited_commit with the repository default-branch HEAD.
Optional freshness.ignore_paths is explicit per audit and only yields current-equivalent when every changed file matches an allowed metadata path.
Non-ignored code/UI/CI changes remain stale and empty compares fail closed.
CI runs the freshness checker and fixture tests.
findings.recommendation: Keep ignore paths narrow; do not add source, CI, release, or security-policy paths merely to suppress stale status.

findings.title: Static workbench sources are duplicated at repository root and under docs/
evidence: The duplicate root index.html, app.js, and styles.css were removed.
docs/index.html, docs/app.js, and docs/styles.css remain the canonical GitHub Pages source.
findings.recommendation: Keep docs/ canonical unless a future build step deliberately generates it from another source.

findings.title: Evidence collector has no dedicated automated tests
evidence: tests/test_audit_tooling.py now covers immutable action refs, private-repository refusal, workflow-run deduplication, HTTP errors, latest-sidecar selection, exact freshness, metadata-only current-equivalent freshness, and fail-closed stale cases.
Portfolio Audit CI runs the fixture tests.
findings.recommendation: Expand fixtures when collector support grows to new evidence types or language-specific adapters.

findings.title: Legacy bootstrap source archive remains in the repository
evidence: The retired .repo-auditor-bootstrap archive and READY marker were removed after confirming no active references.
The archive was incomplete and no longer served the current publication path.
Removal was isolated in a reviewed cleanup branch and preserved in Git history.
findings.recommendation: Do not reintroduce bootstrap archives into the public runtime tree; use normal Git history or release artifacts for recovery.

limitations: The self-audit does not infer or choose a software license on behalf of the repository owner.
GitHub Pages deployment passed, but this recheck did not perform a full cross-browser visual regression suite.
Branch protection and repository administration settings were not evaluated.
The evidence collector has deterministic fixtures but has not been exercised against a large cross-language repository corpus.
recheck_triggers: A LICENSE is added or release/reuse policy changes.
Audit freshness semantics or ignore-path handling changes.
The Pages audit-status UI changes materially.
The evidence collector gains new evidence classes or language-specific adapters.
CI validation or GitHub Pages publication architecture changes.
Publication/IP gate semantics or recommendation rules change.

reasons: No project-specific patent, confidential-input, employer/client/PI-request, or ownership-uncertainty trigger is recorded for repo-auditor.
The missing LICENSE remains a separate reuse-policy finding and is not by itself a reason to make the repository private.
